transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’m here because work has been harder than I want to admit. I keep avoiding the front windows, and even that part of the street outside. I know it sounds kind of silly, but I keep making excuses to stay in the back of the store, even though being up front is part of my job. I just… can’t seem to make myself go over there.
What is it about the front windows or that part of the street that makes you want to avoid it?

It’s just… that area, the windows and the sidewalk right outside, it’s like I can’t get myself to go near it anymore. I know that probably sounds dramatic, and I’m not trying to make it a big thing, but I keep finding reasons to stay in the back of the store instead. Even though I know I’m supposed to be up front sometimes.
Is there something specific that you're afraid of when you're near the front windows or that part of the street?

I don’t know if it’s one specific thing exactly… I just get this really strong feeling that I need to stay away from those windows and that part of the sidewalk. Like if I’m near it, I can’t relax or do my job normally. So I end up making excuses to be in the back instead, even though I know that’s not really okay.
Is there something in particular that you're afraid might happen if you go near the front windows or that part of the street?

I guess… I’m not sure I can put it into one specific thing. It’s more like if I go near the front windows or that same part of the street, I just freeze up and feel like I need to get away from it. So I keep making excuses to stay in the back, even though I know that’s part of my job and I probably shouldn’t be doing that.
Is there something outside the window or on that part of the street that you're afraid of?

Not like a specific person or thing, I don’t think. It’s more that just seeing that spot outside the windows makes me… I don’t know, I can’t make myself go over there anymore. I keep trying to act normal, but I end up making excuses to stay in the back of the store instead, even though I know being up front is part of my job. I’m sorry, I know that probably doesn’t answer it perfectly.
Is there something that happened in the area you're avoiding that might be causing your fear?

Yeah… I mean, I think so. I came in because I just can’t really make myself go near the front windows or that part of the street anymore. I keep finding reasons to stay in the back instead, even though I know being up front is part of my job. I’m not trying to be difficult or anything… it just feels like I can’t do it right now.
Did something upsetting or traumatic happen to you in the area you're avoiding near the front windows or on that part of the street?

Yeah… I think that’s what it is. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is, but after what happened there, I just can’t get myself to go near the front windows or that part of the street anymore. I keep making excuses to stay in the back, even though I know that’s part of my job. I’m sorry if I’m not explaining it very well.
Did you think you were in danger of being hurt or killed when the upsetting event happened near the front windows or on that part of the street?

I’m… not completely sure how to answer that. In the moment I know I felt really scared, but I don’t know if I was specifically thinking, like, “I’m going to die” or anything. I don’t want to overstate it. It just felt dangerous, I guess… if that makes sense?
Can you tell me more about what happened near the front windows or on that part of the street that's causing you to avoid it?

I guess… since then, I just can’t make myself go near the front windows, or that part of the street outside. I know that probably sounds silly, and I’m not trying to avoid work, but I keep finding excuses to stay in the back instead. Even when I know I’m supposed to be up front, I just kind of freeze up and try to get someone else to do it. Does that make sense?
Do you ever have episodes where you feel an intense fear or discomfort that reaches a peak within minutes?

Um… I don’t think so? Not like a sudden episode that peaks really fast, at least not that I’ve noticed. I do get really uncomfortable sometimes, but I’m not sure it’s that kind of thing. Is that what you mean?
Do you find yourself trying to avoid thinking or talking about what happened near the front windows or on that part of the street?

Yeah… I think I do, at least some. I don’t really like talking about it, because it makes me feel kind of embarrassed, like I should be able to just do my job. I mostly notice it with the front windows or that part of the street—I keep finding reasons to stay in the back instead. I’m not trying to make a big deal out of it, but I guess I am avoiding it.
Do you have memories or thoughts about what happened near the front windows or on that part of the street that come into your mind when you don't want them to?

Yeah… a little. I mean, I try not to make it a big thing, but the crash kind of pops into my head when I’m not trying to think about it. Like if I’m setting up displays near the front, suddenly I can hear that bang again, and I see the glass coming down for a second like it’s happening right then. It’s… embarrassing, honestly. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
How long have you been avoiding the front windows and that part of the street outside?

Um… I guess it’s been about two weeks now. Pretty much since the car came through the store window during that overnight shift. I know that probably sounds like kind of a long time to still be weird about it, but… yeah, about two weeks.
Has avoiding the front windows and that part of the street outside been causing you any problems in your daily life or relationships?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it is starting to mess with work. I had to leave in the middle of doing a window reset because I just couldn’t finish it. I felt really stupid about it.

And now I’m kind of worried that I can’t handle the parts of my job that involve the storefront at all, which… I know is basically part of my job. Is that what you mean by causing problems?
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with friends or family because of your avoidance of the front windows and that part of the street?

Not really with friends or family, I don’t think. I mean, I haven’t noticed anything big there. It’s more been work stuff… like I had to leave in the middle of a window reset because I couldn’t finish it, and now I’m worried I’m not going to be able to handle the storefront parts of my job. If that counts.
Have you been avoiding social activities or spending time with friends and family because of what happened at the store?

I don’t think I’ve really been avoiding friends or family, no. It’s more… I came in because I just can’t make myself go near the front windows or that part of the street anymore. At work I keep finding excuses to stay in the back, which I know isn’t great because that’s part of my job.

So, socially, not really, I guess. It’s more the store stuff. Is that still helpful to say?
How much distress or impairment would you say your avoidance of the front windows and that part of the street has caused you?

I’d say… moderate, I guess? I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s definitely affecting work. I had to leave in the middle of a window reset because I just couldn’t finish it, and that was embarrassing.

Now I keep worrying that I won’t be able to handle the storefront parts of my job at all, which is kind of a big deal in retail. So… yeah, it’s causing problems, mostly at work. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you find yourself trying to avoid places, people, or activities that remind you of the car crash at the store?

Yeah… I guess I am. I don’t like saying it like that, but I can’t really make myself go near the front windows anymore, or that part of the street outside the store.

At work I keep finding little reasons to stay in the back instead, even though I know the storefront stuff is part of my job. I’m trying not to make a big deal out of it, but… yes, I think I am avoiding those places.
